title: Using HREBSD to Measure Strain of Second Phase Particles in Aluminum Alloy 2219
content: Brittle fracture of iron-bearing second-phase particles in aluminum alloys is a void nucleation mechanism that plays an important role in ductile failure. The specific mechanism by which stresses develop within particles is not well understood. The objective of this study is to correlate accumulation of geometrically necessary dislocations with stresses in these second-phase particles using high-resolution electron backscatter diffraction (HREBSD). This objective serves to improve current understanding of ductile failure in these alloys.
